title: Renewing the Agreement in Moab
overview: Moses calls a new generation of Israel to renew their binding agreement with God, warns what turning away would bring, and ends by setting what is known apart from what only God knows.

parts.label: Remembering what they saw (vv. 1-8)
parts.note: In Moab, Moses renews with a new generation the covenant (a binding agreement with God) first made at Mount Sinai, here called Horeb. He points to Egypt, the desert years when their clothes and sandals did not wear out, and recent victories, yet says they still have not truly understood it all.

parts.label: Everyone stands together (vv. 9-15)
parts.note: Leaders, women, children, foreigners living among them, and even the lowest laborers who cut wood and carry water are all included in the oath. It also binds people not present that day, usually understood as future generations, though some think it also covers those absent from the gathering.

parts.label: The danger of quiet betrayal (vv. 16-21)
parts.note: A poisonous plant growing in the community pictures one person or group secretly turning to other gods, especially someone who thinks the oath keeps them safe while they do as they please. The phrase pairing wet and dry ground likely means ruin spreading to everyone, though its exact sense is uncertain, and the warning of no forgiveness is stated starkly.

parts.label: A ruined land explained (vv. 22-28)
parts.note: Future generations and foreigners will see the land burned and barren like Sodom and Gomorrah, and the answer given is that the people abandoned the covenant and were driven into another land. The closing words speak as if this exile is already a present fact, which leads many scholars to think the chapter was written or shaped during Israel's exile.

parts.label: Hidden and revealed (v. 29)
parts.note: Some things, such as the future or the full reasons behind events, belong to God alone. What has been made known is given to the people and their children to live by.

disagreement: Christians differ on what verse 4 means when it says God had not yet given the people an understanding heart: some read it as God deliberately withholding that gift until his chosen time, while others read it as a sad comment on the people's own unwillingness to see.
think: When a group shares a commitment, how much can one person's private choices shape what happens to everyone else?
